title: ECS task startup, health, and replacement
objectives: Distinguish task placement, startup, RUNNING state, container health, and ALB target health.
Separate ECS execution-role actions from application task-role permissions.
Diagnose replacement loops by locating the failing lifecycle stage.
assumptions: Illustrative ECS service desired count is two; animation timing is not an AWS guarantee.
Task A starts but the configured ALB readiness path returns HTTP 404.
Task B image pull fails because its execution role lacks the required permission.
A service replacement uses the same task-definition revision until an operator changes it.
hinglish: ECS desired count maintain karta hai, par RUNNING ka matlab healthy target nahi. Image pull, process startup, container health aur ALB probe alag stages hain. Failure ka exact reason pakdo; same bad revision ko replace karne se loop repeat hota hai. Execution role task setup ke liye hai; task role app calls ke liye.

checkpoints.prompt: Task is RUNNING. Can the ALB route user traffic to it?
options: Not until it is registered and passes target health
Only if the execution role can write logs
checkpoints.feedback: Correct. RUNNING is process state; ALB target registration and health are separate gates.

checkpoints.prompt: What evidence distinguishes image startup failure from a running but unhealthy target?
options: Stopped reason and task events versus ALB target reason, port, path, and network rules
checkpoints.feedback: Correct. Use lifecycle-specific evidence; desired count does not identify the failing stage.
